# Three-Tier Partner Program for a Security SaaS ($50k ACV)

A $50k ACV supports meaningful partner margins and real enablement investment, but not unlimited discounting. The design below rewards partners for **sourcing deals** and **building security expertise**, not just processing orders.

## Program goals
- Make partners a material source of new ARR (a common 2-3 year target is 20-30%)
- Concentrate investment in a small number of high-performing partners
- Keep partners attached through renewals, not only the first sale

## Tier summary

| | **Registered** | **Silver** | **Gold** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ideal partner** | Referral partners, consultants, new resellers | VARs/MSSPs with an active security practice | Strategic VARs, MSSPs and SIs that deliver services |
| **Annual partner-sourced bookings** | None | $250k (~5 deals) | $1M (~20 deals) |
| **Certified staff** | 1 sales accreditation | 2 sales + 1 technical | 4 sales + 2 technical + 1 implementation |
| **Sourced, registered deal** | 10% referral fee or 15% resale discount | 20-25% | 30-35% |
| **Fulfilment-only deal** | 5% | 10% | 15% |
| **Renewal margin** | 5% | 10% | 15% |
| **MDF** | None | Proposal-based, up to ~$10k/yr | 3-5% of prior-year bookings |
| **Demo/NFR** | Shared demo tenant | 1 NFR tenant | Multiple NFR tenants + lab |
| **Your coverage** | Pooled/digital channel team | Shared channel manager | Dedicated channel manager + partner SE |

At $50k ACV, a Gold sourced deal yields roughly $15-17.5k of partner margin. That is usually cheaper than a direct-sourced deal once you count AE, SDR and marketing cost. Cap the total stacked discount (partner margin + deal-desk discount) so ASP doesn't erode.

## Benefits by tier

**Registered**
- Partner portal, on-demand training, standard collateral
- Deal registration with 90-day protection
- Referral fee paid when the customer pays

**Silver** (everything in Registered, plus)
- Higher margins and priority deal-reg approval
- Presales support from your SEs for demos and POCs
- Partner locator listing and co-branded campaign templates
- Annual joint business plan with quarterly check-ins
- Eligibility for overflow leads in their territory or vertical

**Gold** (everything in Silver, plus)
- Dedicated channel manager and partner SE
- First access to passed leads and structured co-selling with your direct team
- MDF for events, webinars and demand generation
- Authorisation to deliver implementation and managed services
- Partner Advisory Council seat, roadmap previews, beta access
- Executive sponsor, joint PR and case studies
- Quarterly business reviews against the joint plan

## Security-specific requirements
Security buyers judge you by your partners, so add quality gates beyond revenue:
- **Technical certification** covering deployment, integrations (SIEM, IdP, EDR) and incident-handling basics
- **Gold only:** a signed data-handling agreement, evidence of their own security posture (e.g., SOC 2 or ISO 27001 for MSSPs touching customer data) and a named escalation contact
- **Customer outcomes for Gold:** CSAT of 8/10 or higher and at least 85% gross renewal on partner-managed accounts

## Deal registration and rules of engagement
- First qualified registration wins: named customer, use case, decision maker, timeline
- Approve or reject within 2 business days
- 90 days of protection, plus one 30-day extension with documented progress
- Pay direct reps neutrally on partner-sourced deals in their territory so they collaborate instead of competing
- Define what happens with accounts already in your pipeline (typically direct keeps it unless the partner brings a materially new opportunity)

## Tier movement
- Evaluate annually, with a mid-year checkpoint
- Upgrade at the next quarter once criteria are met
- Downgrades get a two-quarter grace period and a remediation plan
- Count sourced bookings at 100% and fulfilment bookings at 50% toward tier thresholds, so partners are rewarded for creating demand

## Sizing the program
Aim for a pyramid: roughly 5-10 Gold, 20-40 Silver, and an open Registered tier. Too many Gold partners dilutes MDF and channel-manager attention, and Gold stops meaning anything.

## Metrics to track
- Partner-sourced pipeline and ARR, and their share of the total
- Win rate and sales cycle, partner vs. direct
- Time from signing to first deal (target under 120 days)
- Active partner ratio (at least one deal in the trailing 12 months)
- Renewal rate on partner-managed customers
- Deal-reg approval time and conflict rate

## Common pitfalls
- **Resale discounts without deal registration:** causes margin leakage and channel conflict
- **Treating MSSPs like resellers:** they usually need monthly, consumption-based pricing, so consider a separate MSSP track
- **Ignoring direct-sales comp:** misaligned compensation is the most common reason partner programs stall

If it helps, I can turn this into a partner-facing program guide or a margin model.
pc-d2:
# 30-60-90 Day Plan: Onboarding a New Reseller in Germany

**Goal by Day 90:** a certified partner selling independently, with qualified pipeline, at least one closed or late-stage deal, and an agreed plan for the next two quarters.

## Before Day 1
- Reseller agreement signed (with German-language terms if they need them for end customers)
- Transaction path confirmed: buying directly from you, or through a distributor such as ALSO, TD SYNNEX or Ingram Micro
- EUR price list, discount schedule, payment terms and VAT handling (reverse charge for cross-border B2B) settled
- Partner manager and partner SE named on your side; an executive sponsor and sales lead named on theirs

## Days 1-30: Foundation and Enablement
**Objective:** get the partner equipped, compliant and focused.

**Kickoff (ideally in person)**
- Send a detailed agenda in advance; German partners generally value structure, punctuality and written follow-up
- Agree on target segments (e.g., Mittelstand manufacturers in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg), verticals and ideal customer profile
- Draft a joint business plan (JBP) with revenue targets, certification goals and marketing activities

**Compliance pack**
Germany is one of Europe's most privacy-sensitive markets. Give the partner, ready to use:
- Data processing agreement (Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag, AVV) template
- Technical and organisational measures (TOMs), sub-processor list and hosting location (EU or German hosting is a real advantage)
- Your position on international transfers (EU-US Data Privacy Framework, SCCs)
- Certifications: ISO 27001, SOC 2, and BSI C5 if targeting public sector or healthcare
- A works council (Betriebsrat) information pack if the product processes employee data, since co-determination can add months to a deal

**Systems and enablement**
- Portal, deal registration, quoting and NFR/demo environment access
- Sales certification for at least 2 reps; technical certification for 1-2 presales engineers
- German-language pitch deck, one-pager, competitive battlecards and pricing calculator

**Pipeline groundwork**
- Map 15-25 target accounts from the partner's existing customer base
- Agree on rules of engagement for any overlap with your direct pipeline

**Day 30 milestones:** JBP signed off, first certifications complete, target accounts agreed, all systems live.

## Days 31-60: Activation and First Pipeline
**Objective:** generate qualified opportunities and build selling confidence.

- **Co-selling:** join the partner on first customer meetings; your SE leads demos while their SEs shadow, then swap roles
- **Launch campaign:** German-language webinar or roundtable for their customers, an email campaign and a joint LinkedIn or press announcement
- **Events:** pick relevant trade shows (e.g., it-sa for security, Hannover Messe for industrial) and regional IHK or industry association events
- **MDF:** fund one targeted demand-generation activity with clear lead goals
- **Deal registration:** register and qualify the first opportunities; approve within 48 hours
- **Cadence:** weekly 30-minute pipeline call plus technical office hours

**Day 60 milestones:** 5-8 registered opportunities, pipeline of at least 3x the first-quarter target, partner delivering demos on their own.

## Days 61-90: Independence and First Wins
**Objective:** move from assisted to self-sufficient selling.

- Partner runs discovery, demos and POCs independently, with your SE as escalation
- Push the most advanced deal to close, with executive alignment and commercial support where justified
- Finalise the post-sale model: who owns onboarding, implementation, first-line support and renewals
- Certify implementation staff if the partner will deliver services
- Identify a first German reference customer; local references carry real weight with German buyers
- Hold a 90-day business review: results vs. plan, lessons learned, and targets and resourcing for the next two quarters

**Day 90 milestones:** first deal closed or in contract negotiation, 2+ partner-led POCs, at least 3x pipeline coverage for next quarter, a reference candidate identified.

## KPIs to Track

| Metric | Day 30 | Day 60 | Day 90 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Certified sales reps | 2 | 4 | 4+ |
| Certified technical staff | 1 | 2 | 2+ |
| Registered opportunities | 1-2 | 5-8 | 10+ |
| Pipeline coverage | - | 3x Q1 target | 3x next-quarter target |
| Partner-led demos/POCs | 0 | 1-2 | 2+ |
| Closed deals | - | - | 1+ |

## Germany-Specific Tips
- **Expect longer, consensus-driven cycles.** Decisions often involve IT, legal, the data protection officer and sometimes the works council. Have the AVV/TOM pack ready before the first deal hits review.
- **Mind the calendar.** August holidays and late December are slow, and many budgets are set in Q4 for the following year.
- **Don't overpromise.** Reliability and precision build trust faster than enthusiasm; confirm commitments in writing.
- **Localise properly.** Even when the partner's team speaks English, end customers expect German contracts, documentation and support.
- **Protect the partner's investment.** Firm deal-registration protection and no channel conflict with your direct team are what keep a reseller committed after the honeymoon period.

If you share your product category and first-year target, I can tailor the segments, events and KPI numbers.
